9f05d0b104f9da8f0e082e987402cafd7bf68b50.title: Iowa’s November Election Highlights the Importance of Voter Turnout on Local Issues
9f05d0b104f9da8f0e082e987402cafd7bf68b50.description:
Iowa’s move to November bond elections has increased voter participation, but some local measures still draw relatively few voters. Iowa broke its midterm voter turnout record, with preliminary reports showing more than 1.38 million ballots cast, representing 63.4% of registered voters. The statewide constitutional amendment received slightly less participation, with turnout of 56%. While statewide races receive much of the attention, voters also decided important local issues. Two counties voted on the size of their boards of supervisors, nearly 50 bond proposals appeared on local ballots, and communities considered questions involving township governance, library boards, emergency medical services (EMS) taxes, local option sales taxes, and hotel and motel taxes.

The post Iowa’s November Election Highlights the Importance of Voter Turnout on Local Issues appeared first on ITR Foundation.

c0d9132290c08d13b7d6b73defe2af14587b1193.title: Illinois Offers a Warning About Competition
c0d9132290c08d13b7d6b73defe2af14587b1193.description:
The Chicago Tribune editorial board had a lament about Illinois tax policy earlier this summer. They didn’t believe that Illinois was being negligent on tax policy, but “…that our Midwestern neighbors are at least practicing creative taxation thinking.” The editorial should be encouraging for Iowa policymakers. After all, Iowa is one of the states the Tribune points to as an example of a different approach to tax policy. But it should also serve as a warning against complacency. States compete for people, businesses, and investment, and the tax reforms that make Iowa competitive today will not necessarily keep Iowa competitive tomorrow.

The post Illinois Offers a Warning About Competition appeared first on ITR Foundation.
